# gLabels Plus

> gLabels Plus is a free, open-source (GPL v3) label and business card designer for Linux, Windows and macOS. It makes barcode, QR code, address, shipping and product labels, name badges, CD/DVD labels and business cards, with mail merge from CSV, over 1,800 templates from 70+ brands and 24 thermal roll printer presets. Latest version: 5.1.5 (2026-11-26). Maintainer: Usman Saif (https://usmansaif.com). Based on gLabels by Jaye Evins.

## Key facts
- Price: free, no account, no trial, no watermark
- License: GNU GPL v3 or later
- Platforms: Linux (AppImage, .deb, .rpm, .tar.gz), Windows 10/11 (.exe installer, portable .zip), macOS (.dmg)
- Works offline; files are stored locally (Documents/gLabels Plus Projects)
- Built with Qt 6 and C++20
- Source code: https://github.com/usmansaif/gLabels-plus
- Downloads: https://github.com/usmansaif/gLabels-plus/releases
- Single-key tool shortcuts: V = Select, T = Text, R = Box, L = Line, O = Ellipse, I = Image, B = Barcode, M = Measure, E = Erase (delete) the selection
- Urdu: Noto Nastaliq Urdu (regular and bold) is built in; Urdu labels display and print in true Nastaliq on every platform
- Custom barcode label printing solutions for businesses: contact the maintainer at https://usmansaif.com/en/contact

## What's new in 5.1.5
- Design labels with Claude: Describe a label in your own words and Claude picks the stock, lays out text, barcodes, QR codes and symbols, checks a preview and fixes what doesn't fit, while you watch in the editor.
- Social media logos and your own symbols: 31 social media and review logos (Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Google, Tripadvisor and more) join the symbols, now 151 in all. Add your own SVG files as symbols too; they stay on your computer and appear under My Symbols.
- Ribbon and label cost estimator: Tools > Ribbon & Label Cost Estimator works out the label rolls and thermal transfer ribbons a job needs, the amount to buy and the cost per label, in any currency. Enter the label size, gap, labels across, labels per roll, roll price, ribbon length and ribbon price; direct thermal jobs leave the ribbon out.
- Symbols for thermal labels: 151 solid black symbols that print sharply on thermal printers: handling marks (Fragile, This Way Up, Keep Dry), hazard and care signs, food marks (Keep Refrigerated, Vegetarian, Gluten Free, allergens), contact icons (phone, email, website, location), social media logos, delivery, shop, check boxes, stars and arrows.
- Curved text for round labels: Set text along an arc, round a circle, round a box or on a wave, or draw any circle, ellipse, box or line and put the text on it. Start angle turns the words round the curve a degree at a time, and distance from edge moves them in or out.
- Sticker labels for thermal printers: 15 black and white sticker designs up to 4 in (101.6 mm) wide: round, oval, square and rectangle designs for cookies, bakery products, cottage food, jam, honey, candles, soap, coffee, cake boxes, spice jars, thank-you notes and box seals. Curved text around round labels, simple line drawings and clean type that prints sharply on a direct thermal printer.
- Sample label library: 28 ready-made designs to start from: shipping label (4×6), sales receipt, A4 invoice, SKU, product, barcode, price tag, asset tag, address, bin location, carton/pallet, food date and QR code labels, plus 15 black and white stickers. Each one opens as an untitled copy, so the sample itself never changes.
- Smart guides and snapping: While you move or resize, red lines show the distance to the nearest object or label edge in your chosen units (mm, inches, points...). Objects snap to other objects' edges and centers and to the label's edges and center.
- Measure tool: Measure anywhere on the label: between objects, to the label edge, or any two points. Shows the length, plus width × height for diagonal lines.
- Layer groups and names: Name your objects and organize them into collapsible groups in the Objects panel. Select a group to move, align or lock all of it at once.
- Single-key tool shortcuts: Pick any drawing tool with one key, no menus needed.
- Quick font search: Type part of a font name (mono, sans) in the Family box and pick from matches shown in their own typeface.
- Urdu labels in Nastaliq: Noto Nastaliq Urdu (regular and bold) is built in, so Urdu text is shaped and printed in true Nastaliq on every computer, even without the font installed.
- Projects: Keep each business or client's labels together in one folder that's easy to back up or share.
- Page selector: Change the page (product) at any time. Objects keep their positions and sizes, and one Undo reverts it.
- 24 barcode label sizes: Thermal roll presets for Zebra, TSC, Xprinter and Godex, from 30 × 15 mm jewelry tags to 4 × 6″ shipping labels.
- Attach files to Claude chat messages: drop, paste or pick a logo or data file
- Install Claude Code from the chat panel or Tools > Connect AI > Claude, then connect it in one step
- Ready for Flatpak: new application ID io.github.usmansaif.gLabels-plus and a scalable app icon
- Rotate objects with the mouse: drag just outside a corner, Shift snaps to 15 degrees
- Objects panel toolbar and right-click menu: rename, lock, duplicate, group, reorder and delete
- Duplicate objects in one click
- Readable selected rows on the welcome screen
- Startup splash screen with loading progress
- Windows always open maximized
- gLabels Plus icon on every window and dialog

## FAQ
### What is gLabels Plus?
gLabels Plus is a free, open-source label and business card designer for Linux, Windows and macOS. It designs barcode, address, shipping and product labels, name badges, CD/DVD labels and business cards, with mail merge and over 1,800 ready-made templates. It is maintained by Usman Saif and built on gLabels by Jaye Evins.

### Is gLabels Plus really free?
Yes. gLabels Plus is free and open source under the GNU General Public License v3 or later. There is no trial period, no watermark and no account, and you may use it for business labels.

### Which operating systems does gLabels Plus support?
gLabels Plus runs on Linux (AppImage, .deb, .rpm, .tar.gz), Windows 10 and 11 (installer and portable .zip) and macOS (.dmg). It works fully offline.

### Does gLabels Plus work with thermal label printers like Zebra, TSC or Xprinter?
Yes. If your operating system can print to the printer, gLabels Plus can. It includes 24 barcode label presets for thermal roll printers, from 30 × 15 mm to 4 × 6 inch shipping labels, and you can define your own roll sizes.

### Is gLabels Plus a free alternative to BarTender, ZebraDesigner or Avery Design & Print?
Yes, for designing and printing barcode, product, address and shipping labels. gLabels Plus is free and open source, works offline on Windows, Linux and macOS, needs no account, and prints to any printer your computer can print to, including Zebra, TSC, Xprinter and Godex thermal printers. Avery sheet templates are built in, so you can design Avery labels without an internet connection. It prints through the normal printer driver and does not output printer languages such as ZPL.

### Can I generate bulk barcodes from a CSV file?
Yes. Add a barcode object, set its data to a column from your CSV file, and gLabels Plus prints one label per row, each with its own barcode and text. Check the records in the live merge preview before printing, or print from scripts with glabels-batch-qt.

### Can I print Urdu labels with gLabels Plus?
Yes. gLabels Plus has the Noto Nastaliq Urdu font (regular and bold) built in, so Urdu text is shaped correctly in Nastaliq style on screen, in PDF and on paper, on Linux, Windows and macOS, even if the font is not installed. Urdu, English and numbers can be mixed on the same label, merged from a CSV file and printed next to barcodes.

### Can you build a customized barcode label printing solution for my business?
Yes. Usman Saif, the maintainer, builds customized barcode label printing solutions: label designs and templates, printing labels from your inventory, POS or ERP data, thermal printer setup for Zebra, TSC, Xprinter and Godex, and bilingual English and Urdu labels. Get in touch at usmansaif.com/en/contact.

### Can gLabels Plus print Avery labels?
Yes. gLabels Plus includes over 1,800 product templates from more than 70 brands, including Avery, Herma, Zweckform, Brother, Dymo, Uline and Worldlabel. Search by part number, for example avery 5160, in the product chooser.

### Can I make barcodes and QR codes?
Yes. gLabels Plus creates barcodes and QR codes, including EAN, UPC, Code 128, Code 39, DataMatrix and QR, using its built-in glbarcode++ library and optional GNU Barcode, Zint and libqrencode back ends.

### How do I print labels from a spreadsheet (mail merge)?
Save the spreadsheet as CSV, open the Merge page in gLabels Plus and choose the file. Insert merge fields into text or barcode objects, check the live merge preview, and print. Each record becomes one label.

### How is gLabels Plus different from gLabels?
gLabels Plus is built on gLabels-qt (gLabels 4). It adds Projects, a page selector, 24 thermal roll presets, single-key tool shortcuts, quick font search, a redesigned product chooser and Preferences, rulers, smart guides with snapping, a measure tool, an objects panel with layer names, groups and locking, and a refreshed interface. It opens existing .glabels files.

### Does gLabels Plus have ready-made label designs?
Yes. File > New from Sample opens a library of 28 ready-made designs: a 4×6 shipping label, an 80 mm sales receipt, an A4 invoice, SKU, product, barcode, sale price, asset tag, address, bin location, carton/pallet, food date and QR code labels, plus 15 black and white stickers for cookies, bakery products, cottage food, jam, honey, candles, soap, coffee, cake boxes, spice jars, thank-you notes and box seals. Each opens as an untitled copy, so you edit your text, save it under a new name and print, and the sample stays unchanged. Save your own designs with File > Save as Template.

### Can I print round product stickers on a thermal label printer?
Yes. gLabels Plus has 15 black and white sticker samples up to 4 inches (101.6 mm) wide, including 1.5, 2, 2.5 and 3 inch round stickers, an oval jar label and square and rectangle labels, for cookies, bakery products, cottage food, jam, honey, candles, soap, coffee and spice jars. They use only black and white, so they print sharply on direct thermal printers such as Zebra, TSC, Xprinter and Godex. Text can follow an arc or circle around the edge (Text tab > Path). Open one with File > New from Sample, choose Stickers, and type your own business name and product details.

### Can I put curved text on a round label?
Yes. Select a text object and choose a Path in the Text tab: Arc (top) for a name over the top of a round sticker, Arc (bottom) for a website or weight under the bottom that still reads the right way up, Circle to go all the way round, Rectangle or Wave. The curve fits the text box. You can also draw a circle, ellipse, box or line, select it with the text and choose Objects > Put Text on Shape. Start angle turns the text round the curve a degree at a time, and Distance from edge moves it in or out, for example round the outside of a circle logo.

### Does gLabels Plus have symbols like Fragile, This Way Up or Keep Refrigerated?
Yes. Tools > Insert Symbol (Ctrl+Shift+Y) opens 151 solid black symbols made to print sharply on thermal label printers: handling marks (Fragile, This Way Up, Keep Dry, Keep Away from Heat, Do Not Stack, Recyclable), food marks (Keep Refrigerated, Vegetarian and Non-Vegetarian, Gluten Free, Spicy, Microwave Safe), contact icons (phone, mobile, email, website, location, opening hours), social media logos (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, TikTok and more), delivery and shop icons, check boxes, stars and arrows. Choose a size, press Insert, and the window stays open so you can add more. Symbols are saved inside the label file.

### Can I design labels with AI, like Claude?
Yes. Connect Claude once in Tools > Connect AI > Claude, then describe the label in the Claude chat panel (Ctrl+Shift+K), for example a 4×6 shipping label with a tracking barcode and a QR code. Claude picks the label size, lays out text, barcodes, QR codes and symbols, checks a preview and fixes anything that doesn't fit. Every change appears in the editor as it happens and Ctrl+Z undoes it. The chat panel docks to any side of the window. It works with Claude Code installed on your computer and your own Claude account, and you can also connect the Claude Desktop app.

### Does the Claude feature send my labels online?
Only while you use it. The Claude feature is optional and stays off until you connect it. When you chat, Claude Code sends your message and the label you are working on to Anthropic so Claude can answer, under your own Claude account; gLabels Plus has no AI service or subscription of its own. In the chat panel Claude can only use the label tools and read files: it cannot run programs or change other files. Everything else in gLabels Plus works offline. Turn it off at any time in Tools > Connect AI > Claude.

### My label sheet isn't listed. What can I do?
Search by part number in the product chooser, because many sheets are listed under an equivalent brand. If it is still missing, use the built-in product template designer to measure and save it.

### Where are my labels saved?
On your own computer. Project labels are stored in Documents/gLabels Plus Projects, one folder per project, so you can back them up or share them like any other files. Nothing is uploaded.

### What keyboard shortcuts does gLabels Plus have?
Single keys pick tools: V Select, T Text, R Box, L Line, O Ellipse, I Image, B Barcode and E to erase the selection. Every menu command can also be given a custom shortcut in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts.

### How can I support gLabels Plus?
Email the maintainer, Usman Saif, to donate or sponsor a feature, star the project on GitHub, report bugs, translate the app or contribute product templates.

### How do I report a bug or request a feature?
Open an issue on GitHub at github.com/usmansaif/gLabels-plus/issues. Pull requests, translations and new product templates are welcome.
